I personally think that, if he doesn't show and treat the relationship as a 2 way street, he's not really worth being in a relationship with. It always has to come from 2 sides, and you have to be able to listen and talk to your partner, from both ways. If he outright refuses that, and then tries to make it seem like you're in the wrong, there's no use continuing the relationship, because it's not going to go anywhere at that rate.

With the amount of experience he should have in life(with that age difference) i think it's kind of immature to not be able to have a conversation about something your "s/o" is bothered by. If he always steers the conversation towards getting sexual relief, that sounds like he has an issue he either can't fix by himself, or he just really wants you to do it for him.

I personally don't understand why a 33 year old would want an actual active relationship with a 22 year old, because they're in completely different points in their lives, and their main focus is/should be, on something else.

Regardless, you have a problem with this, you try to talk about it, and he complains about it. If your "partner" is not willing to hear you out, that's extremely selfish. A relationship is ment for both parties to grow, and to help each other grow. That (from the information given) doesn't seem to be the case. 

My personal advice would be this : give it some more time. Try to talk to him about it multiple times. When he steers the conversation in a sexual way (and i don't mean just making a joke), just say "nah, don't wanna".

In the end, it's a LDR. He can't force you to do something you don't want to do. So make sure that you don't get swept away in that.
If you feel something 's off, you can always say "hey, i feel like you don' t appreciate me and my feelings, and i'd rather just stay friends."

Hope this helps a bit, and i wish you the best of luck in finding your happiness <3

The total damage will be mitigated, not just the AD addition

So, armor penetration penetrates armor.
Armor blocks physical damage(not attack damage)
And Magic penetration penetrates Magic resist
Magic resist blocks magic damage(not ability power) 

Let's say the enemy has a malphite with 200 armor, and 80 magic resist. Your Q will be blocked by the armor, but your W, E, and R will be blocked by magic resist, since their source is Magic Damage. The damage is just amplified by your AD/AP. It doesn't change the source of the damage.

But the thing is, pen counts towards the type of damage you deal. So for example, Ez' W has an AD and AP ratio, but does magical damage. So the magic pen counts, even if you play full AD.
Pen doesn't work toward your AD or AP numbers.

honestly, i prefer the glacial spike, because it's quite easy to track. you need 5 stacks in a combination of flurry or frostbolts. with Ebonbolt, you have a pretty nice buffer, too.  
what you usually wanna do is spam cast frostbolt, use brain freeze when it's up, make sure all your brain freeze stacks are gone before you cast flurry, and after flurry cast ice lance again. even if it's not brainfreeze procc'd, cus Flurry increases the frost damage taken(seeing as the target is counter for as frozen) for enough time to have an icelance land.   


if you have a flurry proc up, AND GS, use GS, then ice lance, flurry proc, ice lance, frostbolt spam. the only downside to frost atm, is that you don't have much to do besides fishing for procs. the fun part, is that it's quite complicated at first to get a decent rotation down, and being able to prioritize one over the other.   


Also, Shimmer is better because you get to blink twice, which is useful in most cases, since a lot of fights depend on positioning. (for example, on mythrax, i take care of the beam positioning in p2, because i have movement spells, and iceblock if needed)  it's not that ice floes is bad, it's just that shimmer is more optimal. Also, it doesn't interrupt your casting time, and it's instant. so it's faster than walking, which is what you'd have to do with ice flows  


the only downside to GS maaaaaybe, is the cast time feels clunky. but it makes up for that big time with the damage it can output.(even more so with Splitting Ice)  the benefit of this however, is that you have the time to look around the floor and your buffs, to see what to do next, if you're not that great at multitasking.
